# Check gates

A **check gate** is one automatic answer to "is this still true?". There are 47 of them,
and every one keeps the same contract: exit 0 with one summary line, exit 1 with one
finding per line on stderr, exit 2 on misuse.

Everything here is built from [`gates.json`](../data/gates.json). Edit that file, run
`make gates`, and commit both: **Gate reference in sync** fails if they disagree, and
**Gate registry in sync** fails if the registry and the Makefile, the workflow or the
triage page disagree.

## Run them

Every gate below, every finding in one pass:

```bash
make validate
```

Only the gates that read what your branch changed:

```bash
make validate-changed
```

The deterministic repairs, applied rather than reported — **Context layers** and **Page
frontmatter**:

```bash
make fix
```

One gate on its own:

```bash
make gate G=check-types
```

`FAILFAST=1 make validate` stops at the first red gate; `JOBS=n` sets how many run at
once. A red gate's section in [Triage a red gate](triage.md) says what each of its
findings means.

## Where a gate can run

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `local` | runs from a make target on your own machine — `local_command` is what the driver spawns, `local_target` the target that owns it (default `validate`) |
| `ci` | runs as a named step of the change workflow, on every push to main and every pull request |

Every gate CI runs also runs from `make`, so a green `make validate` means CI has nothing
left to tell you.

## Required status checks

A protected branch requires the change workflow's gate-holding jobs in
`.github/workflows/validate.yml` — the job names are the check names:

- `validate`
- `site`

## Each one

### <a id="typecheck"></a>Type check

- **Protects:** The gates, generators and driver compile — every one of them runs through tsx, which strips types without checking them.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Type check`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-types`
- **Fix:** Fix the code at the file and line the finding names; the TS code in the message is the compiler's own.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#type-check](triage.md#type-check)

### <a id="json-sanity"></a>JSON sanity

- **Protects:** Every JSON file git can see parses, and every data file under docs/data/ opens with its source header — version, updated, note, in that order.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `JSON sanity`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-json`
- **Fix:** Repair the file at the line named — usually a trailing comma or a comment; a data file also opens with version, updated and note, in that order.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#json-sanity](triage.md#json-sanity)

### <a id="build-untracked"></a>Built output untracked

- **Protects:** No built output is tracked — no .html, nothing under site/dist/, site/.astro/ or site/coverage/, no site/public/kb.js, and under site/src/content/docs/ only the hand-written home — and .gitignore keeps all seven build paths out.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Built output untracked`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-build-untracked`
- **Fix:** git rm --cached the path the finding names, or restore the missing .gitignore line; the site is built from docs/, so a tracked copy only goes stale.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#built-output-untracked](triage.md#built-output-untracked)

### <a id="gates-sync"></a>Gate registry in sync

- **Protects:** The registry, the Makefile, the change workflow, the triage page and the gate programs on disk agree both ways: every step is registered, every registration runs.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Gate registry in sync`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-gates-sync`
- **Fix:** Make the side the finding names agree with the registry: add the row, the step, the Makefile target or the triage section — or rename it back.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#gate-registry-in-sync](triage.md#gate-registry-in-sync)

### <a id="gates-fresh"></a>Gate reference in sync

- **Protects:** Everything generated from this registry — the gate reference, the triage page's symptom table and every gate count — cannot be hand-edited away from it.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Gate reference in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-gates ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make gates`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#gate-reference-in-sync](triage.md#gate-reference-in-sync)

### <a id="test-colocation"></a>Test colocation

- **Protects:** Every module under tools/src and every hook under .claude/hooks has a test, or an allowlist entry that says why not.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Test colocation`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-test-colocation`
- **Fix:** Write the sibling test, import the module from a suite in its folder, or add a reasoned entry to docs/data/allow/test-colocation.json; delete an entry that excuses nothing.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#test-colocation](triage.md#test-colocation)

### <a id="context-layers"></a>Context layers

- **Protects:** Every governed top-level directory carries a CLAUDE.md within its budget, with a Don't heading and a repo link; the root stays within its budget; every layer link resolves; no layer copies a long root line; and no CLAUDE.md sits anywhere the allowlist does not excuse.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Context layers`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-claude-md`
- **Fix:** Write the missing layer; move a fact out of an over-budget layer to its single source and leave a link; fix the dead link; delete the copied root line. make fix opens a missing heading, and only a person fills it.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#context-layers](triage.md#context-layers)

### <a id="claims"></a>Command claims

- **Protects:** Every command in a shell-labelled fence of the top-level markdown, the pages under docs/ and the harness files still resolves: each make target is in the Makefile, each make gate G=<stem> names a gate or generator, each program path a runner runs is on disk.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Command claims`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-claims`
- **Fix:** Rewrite the command to what the tree now holds, in the change that moved it; never delete the claim to make it pass. A line that must not be judged ends with # claim-ok.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#command-claims](triage.md#command-claims)

### <a id="inbox-cap"></a>Trap inbox cap

- **Protects:** docs/inbox.md keeps its exit ladder under the exact line "## When an entry leaves" and at most 20 entries, each a top-level bullet opening with a bold phrase and at most 8 lines long.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Trap inbox cap`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-inbox`
- **Fix:** Retire an entry by the ladder under "When an entry leaves" in docs/inbox.md, deleting it in the change that lands its new home; give a plain bullet its bold phrase, or move a long entry's detail to its home.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#trap-inbox-cap](triage.md#trap-inbox-cap)

### <a id="harness-shape"></a>Harness shape

- **Protects:** Every folder directly under .claude/ has a row in the one folder list, and every entry holds its type's shape: a skill's description carries a trigger and a boundary and its body the gap, numbered steps and a closing Done means list; an agent declares its tools and its reply shape, the two verifiers exactly Read, Glob and Grep; a rule carries its description and paths; a hook is executable, exits 0, prints nothing and finishes within its wired timeout on unreadable input, and is wired in .claude/settings.json.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Harness shape`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-harness`
- **Fix:** Give the entry the shape the finding names: a row in CLAUDE_DIRS for a new folder, a one-line "Use when … Not for …" description, numbered steps and a closing Done means list, a reply section, exactly Read, Glob and Grep on a verifier, the executable bit, silence and a quick exit for a hook, its wiring in .claude/settings.json. The allowlist ships empty: an entry needs a reason, an owner and a since date, and one that excuses nothing is deleted.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#harness-shape](triage.md#harness-shape)

### <a id="harness-routes"></a>Harness routes

- **Protects:** Every harness file the folder list says to read routes to a live path: each repo-relative link resolves against the linking file, and a path untracked by design is named only beside the command that makes it exist — scratch space such as tmp/ never; every shell command a harness file or CLAUDE.md layer names (any line of a shell fence; a known program in an unlabelled fence or code span) is on permissions.allow or on the prompt-kept list with its reason; and no allow entry lets a write run with no prompt.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Harness routes`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-harness-routes`
- **Fix:** Point the dead link at the file's new home, or drop the sentence with it; name the command that makes an untracked path beside the path, or route the session somewhere tracked. A tool's own folder under tmp/ gets its own row in UNTRACKED, with its command. A named command on neither list goes on permissions.allow when it is read-only or a repo script, else in PROMPT_KEPT with its reason and in the working-in-this-repo.md table. An allow entry that reaches a write is dropped or narrowed to a read.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#harness-routes](triage.md#harness-routes)

### <a id="frontmatter"></a>Page frontmatter

- **Protects:** Every markdown file under docs/ opens with the block its regime asks for: a page declares title, description, area, owner, tags and status, each once and no key outside the page block, each value inside its closed list, its title equal to its H1 and its tags an inline list; status has no default, so a draft never passes for a finished page; an exercise only the exercise keys; and no file sits under docs/records/, because dated records are not kept.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Page frontmatter`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-doc-frontmatter`
- **Fix:** Add the key the finding names, put its value inside its closed list, or keep one line of a key declared twice. make fix adds title from the H1 and owner from git, and a placeholder for any other key, status included, which stays a finding until you answer it.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#page-frontmatter](triage.md#page-frontmatter)

### <a id="docs-style"></a>Page shape

- **Protects:** Every published page keeps the page shape, PAGE-001 to PAGE-008 of docs/reference/page-rules.md but PAGE-007: an intro before the first H2, headings to H3, one H1, a description of at most 160 characters on one line, no raw URL in prose, and at most one Next steps footer, last, holding one link.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Page shape`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-docs-style`
- **Fix:** Follow the rule the finding names; its link opens the rule on docs/reference/page-rules.md.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#page-shape](triage.md#page-shape)

### <a id="kb-shape"></a>KB page shape

- **Protects:** Every page keeps the KB's own rules, KB-001 to KB-016 of docs/reference/page-rules.md: it sits where its structure row says under a slug of its own, and a kind page's blocks, suffixes, section facts, ids, sketch languages, explain block and KB keys follow docs/data/content-model.json.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `KB page shape`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-kb-shape`
- **Fix:** Follow the rule the finding names; its link opens the rule on docs/reference/page-rules.md. Change a page through node scripts/kb.mjs where a writer exists. A page awaiting its explain or description rewrite sits in an entry of docs/data/allow/kb-shape.json, under the ratchet its `covers` names; delete an entry that excuses nothing.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#kb-page-shape](triage.md#kb-page-shape)

### <a id="docs-map"></a>Docs map

- **Protects:** Every page under docs/ is one link from docs/README.md, or two through a hub it links, and every .md link on the map and on those hubs lands on a page that exists. Only the map and docs/CLAUDE.md are exempt.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Docs map`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-docs-map`
- **Fix:** Give the page its row in docs/README.md, or in a hub the map links, in the change that adds the page; point a row at the page's new path, or delete it. A page in docs/data/site-structure.json gets its row from make map.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#docs-map](triage.md#docs-map)

### <a id="map-fresh"></a>Docs map in sync

- **Protects:** The page table inside docs/README.md is the structure file's areas and pages in reading order, rendered by tools/src/gen/gen-map.ts, and cannot be hand-edited away from it.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Docs map in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-map ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make map`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#docs-map-in-sync](triage.md#docs-map-in-sync)

### <a id="mermaid-parse"></a>Diagrams parse

- **Protects:** Every mermaid fence in the markdown under docs/ parses with the mermaid the site build draws with, so a broken diagram fails in seconds here rather than as a placeholder a reader finds, or minutes into make site-build.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Diagrams parse`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-mermaid`
- **Fix:** Fix the diagram at the line the finding names; mermaid's own message says what it expected there.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#diagrams-parse](triage.md#diagrams-parse)

### <a id="repo-links"></a>Repository links

- **Protects:** Every link in the repository's markdown leads somewhere: its file exists inside the repository, a fragment names a heading or an id of its markdown file, and a label that is only a path names the file the link goes to. Fences and code spans hold no links.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Repository links`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-repo-links`
- **Fix:** Point the link at what the tree holds now, in the change that moved it: the file's new path, or the heading's new slug. Make a label that is a path name the file the link goes to.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#repository-links](triage.md#repository-links)

### <a id="vocabulary"></a>Vocabulary bans

- **Protects:** The glossary is sound — every term holds its eight fields, a declared scope and related terms listed on both sides, and each banned phrasing has one owner — and no markdown prose line git lists uses a banned phrasing, outside code, fences, the searcher's words in `solves` and `aliases`, and the lines that opt out with `<!-- vocab-ok -->`.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Vocabulary bans`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-vocabulary`
- **Fix:** Rewrite the line in the word the finding names, choosing it for the sense (through node scripts/kb.mjs for the explain, production and wild blocks). A line that must name the phrasing carries `<!-- vocab-ok -->`; a file that must keep one gets a reasoned entry, with owner and since, in docs/data/allow/vocabulary.json; an entry that excuses nothing is deleted.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#vocabulary-bans](triage.md#vocabulary-bans)

### <a id="glossary-fresh"></a>Glossary reference in sync

- **Protects:** docs/reference/glossary.md is byte for byte what tools/src/gen/gen-vocabulary.ts renders from docs/data/glossary.json, so a word changes in one place and the reference page follows.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Glossary reference in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-vocabulary ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make glossary`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#glossary-reference-in-sync](triage.md#glossary-reference-in-sync)

### <a id="search-synonyms"></a>Search synonyms hold their rules

- **Protects:** Every bridge in docs/data/search-synonyms.json can fire: each key a lowercase word of two letters or more and no stopword, one to four targets with no repeat and no self-reference, every target a word of some page's declared facts; an expansion names no target containing its key, shadows no curated key and keeps key order, and expansionMeta.entries counts the expansions.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Search synonyms hold their rules`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-search-synonyms`
- **Fix:** Edit docs/data/search-synonyms.json as the finding says: drop or replace the target, sort the keys, merge a shadowed expansion into curated, or set expansionMeta.entries to the count. The judgement no gate makes is the kb-vocab skill's.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#search-synonyms-hold-their-rules](triage.md#search-synonyms-hold-their-rules)

### <a id="search-synonyms-fresh"></a>Search synonyms reference in sync

- **Protects:** docs/reference/search-synonyms.md is byte for byte what tools/src/gen/gen-search-synonyms.ts renders from docs/data/search-synonyms.json, so a bridge changes in one place and the reference page follows.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Search synonyms reference in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-search-synonyms ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make synonyms`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#search-synonyms-reference-in-sync](triage.md#search-synonyms-reference-in-sync)

### <a id="search-oracle"></a>Search oracle answers

- **Protects:** Every query in docs/data/search-oracle.json is answered as the case says, by the search box's ranking over the page tree and by kb.mjs find alike (a case marked `via: "cli"` by find alone): the first hit is one of the wished ids, the first n hits are all of the wished kind or band, a page named in `within` is at or above its rank, and at least `min` of the ids a `covers` names are among its first n hits.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Search oracle answers`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-search-oracle`
- **Fix:** Fix the ranking in tools/src/lib/search-score.ts or add the synonym the query needs through the kb-vocab skill, then rerun the gate; a case that names a page that is gone is edited or dropped in docs/data/search-oracle.json. Never lower a `covers` case's `min`, or widen its `n`, to land a change.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#search-oracle-answers](triage.md#search-oracle-answers)

### <a id="kb-record-schema"></a>KB records hold their schema

- **Protects:** Every page's `kb.mjs record` holds the published kb-record/1 schema, and the `--json` of `get`, `related`, `backlinks`, `refs` and `resolve` for every page, of `ls`, `validate` and `graph`, and of `find` and `brief` for every query in docs/data/search-oracle.json holds its schema in kb-cli/1 or kb-graph/1, with every object closed to a key the schema does not list, every key in the order the schema lists it, and each call ending as the contract says: an allowed exit code, nothing on stderr, two-space JSON and one newline.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `KB records hold their schema`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-kb-records`
- **Fix:** Fix the code that printed it (tools/src/kb/record.ts, tools/src/lib/kb-record.ts or tools/src/kb/cli.ts), or, when the code is right and the schema lags, add the key to the schema in tools/src/contract/schema/ in the same change; inside /1 a schema only grows, so a rename, a removal, a changed type or a changed key order is a new major version and never an edit. A schema that is missing or does not compile is restored or repaired first, since no page is read until it holds.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#kb-records-hold-their-schema](triage.md#kb-records-hold-their-schema)

### <a id="products"></a>Product registry

- **Protects:** Every vendor documentation link in docs/data/products.json is named by a mapping cell in its own provider's column of a capability page, is https, and points at documentation rather than a homepage. Whether each URL still answers is make products, which needs the network.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Product registry`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-products`
- **Fix:** Delete an entry no cell names, move one filed under the wrong provider, or fix its URL, in docs/data/products.json.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#product-registry](triage.md#product-registry)

### <a id="relations"></a>Relations closed and paired

- **Protects:** Every typed edge in docs/data/relations.json joins two published pages with one of the closed verbs in docs/data/content-model.json, written once from the first verb of its pair with both sides' notes; no pair carries a verb family twice or both ways round, and every custom group heading, group_order pin and mapped table row resolves.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Relations closed and paired`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-relations`
- **Fix:** Fix the record at the line the finding names in docs/data/relations.json (node scripts/kb.mjs link and unlink write whole edges), then run make gen.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#relations-closed-and-paired](triage.md#relations-closed-and-paired)

### <a id="learning-paths"></a>Learning paths resolve

- **Protects:** Every stage in docs/data/learning-paths.json is a route docs/data/site-structure.json produces, spelled exactly, and no stage is a page that declares status draft; every profile and tour note is a closed record, a profile names the page its tour renders on, and no note sits on a route its profile does not stage.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Learning paths resolve`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-learning-paths`
- **Fix:** Fix the stage or note the finding names in docs/data/learning-paths.json, and move a stage in the same change as its page's structure row; then run make gen.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#learning-paths-resolve](triage.md#learning-paths-resolve)

### <a id="tracks"></a>Tracks resolve

- **Protects:** Every Start-here track in docs/data/tracks.json is a closed record of 3 to 6 themes, each a learning-paths profile id whose theme page is published and not a draft, 4 to 6 tracks in all with unique ids; every tier is intro, core or advanced on a published slug, and every theme a track lists has one.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Tracks resolve`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-tracks`
- **Fix:** Fix the track or tier the finding names in docs/data/tracks.json; a theme must be a published, non-draft theme page with a profile in docs/data/learning-paths.json.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#tracks-resolve](triage.md#tracks-resolve)

### <a id="tour-order"></a>Tour order holds

- **Protects:** In every theme's tour (a profile's stages in docs/data/learning-paths.json), a page comes after each page it requires: for every prerequisite edge in docs/data/relations.json whose two pages are both stages of one profile, the required page has the lower stage index.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Tour order holds`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-tour-order`
- **Fix:** Move the prerequisite's stage above the page the finding names in docs/data/learning-paths.json, keeping its notes (they are keyed by route); or, when the edge is wrong, unlink it in docs/data/relations.json. Then run make gen.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#tour-order-holds](triage.md#tour-order-holds)

### <a id="prerequisites"></a>Prerequisite graph holds

- **Protects:** docs/data/prerequisites.json is a graph a reader can follow: no cycle in what to read first, every id and route resolved, every related pair listed both ways, every record reached by an edge or a learning-path stage, and no stable page requiring a draft one.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Prerequisite graph holds`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-prerequisites`
- **Fix:** The graph is built from docs/data/relations.json, so fix the edge there (node scripts/kb.mjs link or unlink), then make prerequisites — never in prerequisites.json; a finding about an edge names its line in relations.json. An orphan gets an edge or a stage, or an entry with its reason in docs/data/allow/prerequisites.json.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#prerequisite-graph-holds](triage.md#prerequisite-graph-holds)

### <a id="prerequisites-fresh"></a>Prerequisite graph in sync

- **Protects:** docs/data/prerequisites.json and docs/reference/prerequisites.md are byte for byte what tools/src/gen/gen-prerequisites.ts builds from docs/data/relations.json, the pages' titles and descriptions and the structure file: the relations file's second form, held equal to it both ways, so a hand edit to either output, or an edge change without the rebuild, is stale.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Prerequisite graph in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git` · `bash` · `jq` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-prerequisites ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make prerequisites`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#prerequisite-graph-in-sync](triage.md#prerequisite-graph-in-sync)

### <a id="relations-fresh"></a>Relationships blocks in sync

- **Protects:** Every page's relationships block (its relationships marked block) is byte for byte what tools/src/gen/gen-relations.ts renders from docs/data/relations.json, the verbs in docs/data/content-model.json and each page's title, and every page an edge names holds the block's markers: a hand edit to a block, or an edge changed without the rebuild, is stale.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Relationships blocks in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-relations ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make gen`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#relationships-blocks-in-sync](triage.md#relationships-blocks-in-sync)

### <a id="tours-fresh"></a>Tour and fluency blocks in sync

- **Protects:** Every theme's tour block and every member page's fluency block (their tour and fluency marked blocks) are byte for byte what tools/src/gen/gen-tours.ts renders from docs/data/learning-paths.json and each page's title: a hand edit to a block, or a stage or note changed without the rebuild, is stale.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Tour and fluency blocks in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-tours ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make gen`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#tour-and-fluency-blocks-in-sync](triage.md#tour-and-fluency-blocks-in-sync)

### <a id="site-structure"></a>Structure file

- **Protects:** docs/data/site-structure.json stays the one publishing decision: each area has a kebab-case id used once, a label free of an em-dash and a hub (description, intro, tags), and nests only under a declared area; an optional `nav` is `link` (an area with exactly one row, nested under nothing and holding nothing) or `none` (unpublished, and everything nested under it `none` too); each row has a slug, a label, a route no other area or row takes and a source that exists (a page under docs/, a committed site page, or a page the area's generator writes); the area ids match AREAS in site/src/lib/types.ts, both ways and in order; and every hand-written page in the site's input folder is listed. That every learning-path stage is a route the file produces is the learning-paths gate's check.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Structure file`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-site-structure`
- **Fix:** Fix the area or row the finding names in docs/data/site-structure.json, and keep AREAS in site/src/lib/types.ts in the same order.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#structure-file](triage.md#structure-file)

### <a id="tags"></a>Tags

- **Protects:** Every page under docs/ carries its tags as an inline list of 2-5 terms from docs/data/tags.json that apply to its class, in facet order, with exactly one topic first; the tag list itself is sound (facets, one facet per term, a unique label on every topic and on nothing else); the flat TAGS tuple in site/src/lib/types.ts holds the same ids, both ways; and every term is used by some page.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Tags`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git` · `bash` · `jq`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-tags`
- **Fix:** Set a page's tags with node scripts/kb.mjs set <id> --tags '["topic", "skill", …]'. A new term goes into docs/data/tags.json and into the TAGS tuple in site/src/lib/types.ts, with the pages that earn it; then make taxonomy.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#tags](triage.md#tags)

### <a id="tags-fresh"></a>Tag reference in sync

- **Protects:** docs/reference/tags.md is byte for byte what tools/src/gen/gen-taxonomy.ts renders from docs/data/tags.json: every term once, one table per facet, the bounds the tags gate holds.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Tag reference in sync`
- **Needs:** `node` · `diff`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=gen-taxonomy ARGS=--check`
- **Fix:** `make taxonomy`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#tag-reference-in-sync](triage.md#tag-reference-in-sync)

### <a id="site-tokens"></a>Site colour tokens

- **Protects:** Every colour in the site's stylesheets comes from a token: a hex, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() or hsla() literal in any stylesheet under site/src but the token stylesheet site/src/styles/tokens.css is a finding naming its file and line (spec kb.site.components, token-gate).
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site colour tokens`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-site-tokens`
- **Fix:** Replace the literal with Starlight's --sl-color-* or a --kb-* token. A value nothing gives goes into site/src/styles/tokens.css once, under a name, and the stylesheet uses the name.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-colour-tokens](triage.md#site-colour-tokens)

### <a id="site-hooks"></a>Site hook parity

- **Protects:** The site's markup and its behaviour modules name the same data-kb-* hooks: a hook a module queries and no markup emits, or one markup emits and nothing reads, is a finding; a hook kept only for a reader of the built page is excused in docs/data/allow/site-hooks.json with its reason (spec kb.site.components, hook-parity-gate).
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site hook parity`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-site-hooks`
- **Fix:** Rename the hook back on the side that moved, or delete the dead one. A hook that exists only for a person or an agent reading the built page gets an entry in docs/data/allow/site-hooks.json saying who reads it.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-hook-parity](triage.md#site-hook-parity)

### <a id="site-portable"></a>Site portability

- **Protects:** The built site opens from a local folder: no root-absolute link or source, no module script of ours, the page facts in every head, the keyboard walk intact, and a search payload that covers every page but the hubs with anchors that resolve (spec kb.site.offline). The files a machine reader takes match the repo: each page-tree page has its markdown source beside it, byte for byte; each page of the knowledge base has its record, byte for byte what kb.mjs record prints, and a head that links the markdown and the record beside it; graph.json is what kb.mjs graph prints, schema/ holds a copy of each published schema, index.json holds the closed form of kb-index-1 and agrees with the records, llms.txt is the build's and every link in it opens a file, and llms-full.txt is every page's markdown after its marker line.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site portability`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/gates/check-site-portable.ts`
- **Fix:** `make site-build`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-portability](triage.md#site-portability)

### <a id="site-absence"></a>Site noise and data layer

- **Protects:** Every built page carries its knowledge and nothing a machine reader has to wade through (spec kb.noise.absence-gate, with kb.pagedata.two-layers): each page is at the formatter's fixed point, loads one classic kb.js and no inline module, carries no style element, presentational style or inline handler, and keeps every landmark outside the knowledge region skip-marked; no script file ships that nothing loads; a fact sits only on a class-free element carrying nothing but data-* and an id, the knowledge region is one article block with the four page facts and no skip marker, and every title sits in a title block. Every other script, stylesheet and noscript style carries a reasoned entry in its allowlists; anything unnamed fails, and so does an entry that matches nothing. One page, 404.html, is held to its own rule in place of the bundle, stylesheet and style-element ones: it loads no file of the site and carries exactly one small style of its own.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site noise and data layer`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/gates/check-site-absence.ts`
- **Fix:** `make site-build first: the formatter and the post-build pass repair most findings. One that stays is markup a component or the generator writes: fix the component under site/src, or the post-build pass in tools/src/site/site-portable.ts.`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-noise-and-data-layer](triage.md#site-noise-and-data-layer)

### <a id="site-links"></a>Site built links

- **Protects:** Every link in the built site lands on a file on disk and every fragment on an anchor there; every folder of pages has its hub (but a folder holding only the rows of a single-page `link` area), every page but the home page is held by exactly one hub, which lists its area's pages in reading order within each group, and every learning-path stage is a built page (spec kb.gates.link-integrity, site-gate).
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site built links`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/gates/check-site-links.ts`
- **Fix:** `make site-build first: most findings on a stale site go away. One that stays is a page or a hub linking what is not there: fix the page under docs/ (or the structure file, for a hub) and rebuild.`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-built-links](triage.md#site-built-links)

### <a id="site-accessibility"></a>Site accessibility floor

- **Protects:** Every built page holds the accessibility floor markup can answer without a browser (spec kb.noise.accessibility, static-floor): a language on the root, one h1 with no heading before it, aria references that resolve, options inside a listbox, an alt on every image, a name on every graphic that is not hidden, an outline on every hub, a focus ring on every kb control, and page text that is not mostly chrome (80 percent, with a reasoned allowlist that ships empty, and a measured warning band from 70 percent whose page count may not rise above the bandMax in docs/data/allow/site-a11y.json).
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site accessibility floor`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/gates/check-site-a11y.ts`
- **Fix:** `make site-build first. A finding that stays is markup a component or the markdown plugin writes: fix it there (site/src/components, tools/src/lib/site-markdown.ts) and rebuild.`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-accessibility-floor](triage.md#site-accessibility-floor)

### <a id="site-axe"></a>Site accessibility in a browser

- **Protects:** Every built page, opened from disk in headless Chromium in both themes, has no WCAG 2.1 A or AA violation axe-core finds, contrast above all (spec kb.noise.accessibility, browser-floor). The waiver list ships empty; with no browser installed the gate opens nothing, says so and exits 0, unless KB_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 is set (CI's site job sets it), when the missing browser is a finding.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site accessibility in a browser`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/gates/check-site-axe.ts`
- **Fix:** `make site-build first. A contrast finding is a token: fix the colour in site/src/styles/tokens.css, never in a component. Anything else is markup: fix the component or the post-build pass that writes it, and rebuild.`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-accessibility-in-a-browser](triage.md#site-accessibility-in-a-browser)

### <a id="site-budget"></a>Site size budget

- **Protects:** The built site stays inside the sizes it was measured at: any page's HTML raw and gzipped, a tighter raw bound on a page that is not a case study and on a hub, the bundle, the search payload and the manifest raw and gzipped, every record, graph.json, llms.txt and llms-full.txt raw and gzipped, the blocking stylesheets of a page, the gzipped bytes before a page's first render, and the files a page asks for. Every number is in the BUDGETS constant of tools/src/gates/check-site-budget.ts beside the value it was set from.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site size budget`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/gates/check-site-budget.ts`
- **Fix:** `make site-build first. The finding names the file, its size, the budget and the part that grew most: trim that part. Raise a number in BUDGETS only with a new measurement written beside it.`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-size-budget](triage.md#site-size-budget)

### <a id="site-e2e"></a>Site reader flows

- **Protects:** What a reader does on the built site works in a real browser, from disk and from a server, at a desktop and a phone width: home to a hub to a page, the Start here tracks, the sidebar, search, the theme, favourites, practiced marks, hub filters, the prerequisite card, mentioned-by and next steps, the draft chip, the stack map page and its sidebar link, diagrams, code sketches and copy, the keyboard path and the phone menu. Its own run place after make site-build, never inside it; the skipped flows are pinned to docs/data/allow/site-e2e.json, so a new skip or a stale allowance is a finding; with no browser installed the gate runs nothing, says so and exits 0, unless KB_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1 is set (CI's site job sets it), when the missing browser is a finding.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Site reader flows`
- **Needs:** `node`
- **Run it:** `make site-e2e`
- **Fix:** `make site-build first, then make site-e2e. The finding names the flow, the project (file or served, desktop or phone) and the spec line: fix the component that flow drives under site/src/components, or the flow in tools/e2e when the page changed on purpose. A flow asserts what a reader sees, never a class name.`
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#site-reader-flows](triage.md#site-reader-flows)

### <a id="tests-bash"></a>Hook suite (bash)

- **Protects:** The hooks under .claude/hooks keep their contract: the advisory names a command for each kind of owed work and says nothing otherwise, the guard denies only in command position, and both exit 0 on any input. Proven by tests/**/*.test.sh, run through tests/run.sh.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Hook suite (bash)`
- **Needs:** `node` · `bash` · `jq` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-bash-suite`
- **Fix:** Read the failing test file's header, which says what it proves, then the assertion at the named line; bash tests/run.sh <part of its path> -v replays that file with every assertion.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#hook-suite-bash](triage.md#hook-suite-bash)

### <a id="tests-vitest"></a>Gate suite (vitest)

- **Protects:** Every gate, generator and the driver prove pass, fail and misuse in a sandbox, and the suite's coverage stays at or above the floors in tools/vitest.config.ts.
- **Runs:** `make` · `validate.yml` — step `Gate suite (vitest)`
- **Needs:** `node` · `git`
- **Run it:** `make gate G=check-suite`
- **Fix:** Make the named test pass, or cover the new code; never lower a floor in tools/vitest.config.ts to land a change.
- **Triage:** [docs/reference/triage.md#gate-suite-vitest](triage.md#gate-suite-vitest)
